propositions: A configured provider is silently discarded when the model id contains a colon in its version suffix (canonical Bedrock ids like 'us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0' are treated as already-qualified)
The detection of provider-qualified strings uses a colon-presence test that cannot distinguish between a provider separator colon and a colon inside a model id's version component
_resolve_target and infer_provider implement the qualified-string test independently, allowing them to diverge and mishandle the same inputs
An explicitly configured provider can be overridden by punctuation in the model string when guard order is wrong (e.g. _resolve_target('openai:gpt-4o', provider='bedrock') still drops bedrock)
Unversioned Bedrock aliases without colons work correctly, masking the defect for the majority canonical form that AWS publishes
Downstream error messages report a fragment of the model id as a provider name, contradicting the operator's actual configuration and making diagnosis impossible
